title: Specialised Cells and Organisation
seo_title: Year 7 Science: Specialised Cells, Tissues, Organs and Diffusion Worksheets
standard_text: The hierarchical organisation of multicellular organisms: from cells to tissues to organs to systems to organisms; the role of diffusion in the movement of materials in and between cells; the structural adaptations of some unicellular organisms.
meta_desc: Free Year 7 science worksheets on specialised cells and organisation: cells, tissues, organs and organ systems, adapted cells, diffusion and unicellular organisms. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Specialised cells suit their jobs; substances diffuse from high to low concentration.
body_html:
How to think about it

Multicellular organisms are organised in levels.

  • Cells → tissues → organs → organ systems → organism.
  • Specialised cells have features for their jobs, such as the tail of a sperm cell or the long hair of a root hair cell.
  • Substances move in and out of cells by diffusion, from high to low concentration.
Example

The stomach is an?

Made of several tissues

Answer: organ

Example

Oxygen in the lungs moves which way?

High to low

Answer: into the blood

Common mistakes

  • Thinking an organ is smaller than a tissue.
  • Thinking diffusion goes from low to high concentration.
  • Thinking all cells look the same.

faq.q: What are the levels of organisation?
faq.a: Cells group into tissues, tissues into organs, organs into organ systems, and organ systems make up an organism.
A cell with features suited to a particular job, such as a nerve cell that is long to carry messages.
The spreading of particles from where there are many (high concentration) to where there are fewer (low concentration).
